 Who We Are 
 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale. As an award-winning digital product consultancy and the digital division of TELUS, one of Canada’s largest telecommunications providers, we design and deliver transformative customer experiences through cutting-edge technology, agile thinking, and a people-first culture
 With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

 From mobile apps and websites to voice UI, chatbots, AI, customer service, and in-store solutions, TELUS Digital enables seamless, trusted, and digitally powered experiences that meet customers wherever they are — all backed by the secure infrastructure and scale of our multi-billion-dollar parent company.

 Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation 
 Lead a global, multidisciplinary team across multiple concurrent workstreams, ensuring product, engineering, and delivery leaders operate as a cohesive unit to deliver measurable outcomes.

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Qualifications 
 10+ years in the technology industry, including 4+ years in a senior leadership role in a professional services, consulting, or agency environment.

 Proven record managing a diverse portfolio of client accounts (ideally $10M+ in annual revenue) with a focus on retention and organic growth.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

 Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.

 Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.

 Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.

 Experience managing and coaching leaders across Product, Engineering, and Delivery, and leading large, globally distributed teams.

 Strong command of professional services metrics, including gross margin, utilization, forecast accuracy, and effective billable rates.

 Exceptional ability to navigate “recovery situations” and high-stakes client conversations with poise, clarity, and a solution-oriented mindset.

jobs.title: VP, Financial Planning & Analysis
jobs.description:
About ClearGov 

 ClearGov is building the modern financial operating layer for the public sector. 

 We help US local governments and school districts plan, budget, report, and communicate their finances with clarity and confidence. From long-term planning to financial reporting, compliance, and transparency, our platform connects the work finance teams are already doing and makes it easier to deliver for their communities. 

Today, more than 2,000 public sector organizations use ClearGov, and we continue to expand our platform and reach as we grow.

 Our Core Values 

 Be Clear & Credible  

 We are authentic in our interactions, communicating with clarity, speaking with honesty, and following through with consistency. We turn transparency into our greatest competitive advantage. 

 Be Human   

 We are human partners to our colleagues and customers and lead with consideration and kindness - making space for others to do the same. We turn empathy into a shared strength.

 Be Better Together   

 We are committed to building an inclusive community where everyone thrives. We share successes, support each other through challenges, and show up for our teammates the way we show up for our customers. We turn togetherness into our greatest advantage and collaboration into our greatest multiplier.

 Be Honourable/Honorable   

 We are responsible to our colleagues and customers. We bring our full selves to every conversation, every project, every decision, and every relationship. We act with intention, deliver on our commitments, and lead with integrity - even when no one is watching. We turn honour into the foundation that powers everything we do.

 Be Connected 

 We are culture builders where people are seen, welcomed, and celebrated. We show up in every interaction - the laughs, the wins, the hard days. We turn connection into opportunities for people to feel they belong.

 What Makes You a Great Fit 

 You take ownership and follow through

 You communicate clearly and effectively

 You're comfortable solving problems and figuring things out

 You learn quickly and adapt as things change

 You care about the team, not just your own work

 You bring a sense of humor and perspective to what you do

 About the Opportunity 

 We are seeking a hands-on Vice President, Financial Planning & Analysis to own enterprise-wide planning, forecasting, and performance analytics for a growth-stage SaaS business. This is not a purely oversight role, the VP, FP&A will be in the models directly, building and stress-testing scenarios, and translating the numbers into decisions. Reporting to the CFO, this person will be a key partner to executive leadership and business unit owners, and will play a central role in the company's next chapter of growth.

 We're looking for someone who wants to build, not just review, someone as comfortable inside the mechanics of a model as they are presenting its output to the CFO and board. 

 Key Responsibilities: 

 10+ years of progressive finance experience, including FP&A leadership, with a track record of being genuinely hands-on in the model — not several layers removed from it.

 Direct experience in a SaaS or recurring-revenue business, fluent in ARR, NRR, churn, cohort, and unit economics analysis.

 Strong financial modeling and scenario-planning skills — able to build complex models from scratch and pressure-test assumptions in real time.

 Exposure to an exit, sale process, recapitalization, refinancing, or similar transaction, with a working understanding of what "diligence-ready" actually looks like.

 Executive presence — able to move fluidly between deep model work and clear, confident presentation to the CFO and board.

 Strong judgment about what's urgent, what's important, and what can wait — able to prioritize across competing asks from the CFO, business leaders, and the sponsor.

 Nice-to-haves:

 CPA, CFA, or MBA.

 Prior experience building or scaling an FP&A function from a less mature state.

 Compensation:

If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

 Why Join ClearGov 

 Remote and flexible work environment

 Meaningful work that impacts communities across the United States

 Collaborative, high-performing team

 Competitive compensation and benefits

 Opportunities to grow as we scale 

 Benefits 

 Medical, dental & vision insurance

 Sick and safe time off

 Paid parental leave

 Paid bereavement leave

 Paid jury duty + civic service leave

 Employee assistance program

 2 summer days + annual end-of-year "Dimming of the Lights"

 Employee referral bonus program

 How to Apply 
Ready to join us? Apply online today! 

 Equal Opportunity Employer 
ClearGov is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind based on race, color, sex, religion, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, or any other protected characteristic. Hiring decisions are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance. 
 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.  
 Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset. 

 PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office) 
 Fast paced office environment 
 Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: CFO/VP Finance
jobs.description:
Vice President, Finance and 
Administration / Chief Financial Officer

Division: Finance and Administration

Reports To: President

Direct Reports:

• Controller

• Executive Director, Procurement and Administrative Services

• Executive Director, Public Safety

• Executive Director, Facilities Management

• Internal Auditor

 Position Summary 

Our post-secondary education client is seeking an accomplished and 
strategic financial executive to serve as its next Vice 
President, Finance and Administration / Chief Financial Officer.

As the chief financial and administrative officer and a member 
of the President’s Cabinet, the CFO provides executive 
leadership, strategic direction, and institutional stewardship 
for the school's financial operations, administrative services, 
public safety, and facilities.

This position ensures the responsible management of 
institutional resources while advancing the school's mission, 
vision, and strategic priorities. Serving as a trusted advisor 
to the President, the CFO helps shape institutional strategy, 
provides sound financial counsel, and partners with executive 
leadership to maintain the school's fiscal strength, operational 
effectiveness, and long-term sustainability.

The successful candidate will bring an institution-wide 
perspective and contribute to college-wide initiatives, 
organizational culture, governance, strategic planning, and 
executive decision-making.

 Executive Leadership Philosophy 

The school's Vice Presidents serve as institutional leaders 
first and functional leaders second. As members of the 
President’s Cabinet, they share responsibility for advancing the 
school's mission through collaborative leadership, strategic 
planning, innovation, and responsible stewardship of public 
resources.

The CFO will balance financial discipline with innovation, 
operational excellence with exceptional customer service, and 
long-term sustainability with the evolving needs of students, 
employees, and the community.

Success will be measured not only by the performance of assigned 
departments, but also by meaningful contributions to the overall 
effectiveness, reputation, and future of the college.

 Core Executive Responsibilities 

 Cabinet and Strategic Leadership 

• Serve as an active member of the President’s Cabinet and 
executive leadership team.

• Advise the President on strategic, financial, operational, and 
organizational matters.

• Participate in institutional planning, executive 
decision-making, and policy development.

• Collaborate across divisions to advance college-wide 
initiatives and strategic priorities.

• Represent the school before governmental agencies, financial 
institutions, professional organizations, and community 
partners.

• Develop long-range financial and operational strategies that 
support the school’s Strategic Plan.

• Evaluate emerging trends, risks, and opportunities affecting 
higher education and public finance.

• Champion innovation, continuous improvement, and responsible 
resource management.

 Organizational Leadership 

• Recruit, develop, mentor, and evaluate executive leaders and 
management staff.

• Build high-performing teams committed to operational 
excellence and continuous improvement.

• Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, inclusion, 
professionalism, and exceptional customer service.

• Promote employee engagement, leadership development, and 
succession planning.

• Establish measurable goals and performance expectations 
aligned with institutional priorities.

 Stewardship and Governance 

• Ensure responsible stewardship of the college’s financial, 
physical, and operational resources.

• Support the Board of Regents through executive reports, 
recommendations, and presentations.

• Develop and implement policies, administrative regulations, 
and business practices that strengthen institutional 
effectiveness.

• Ensure compliance with federal and state laws, accreditation 
standards, Board policies, and administrative regulations.

• Maintain effective systems of internal control, enterprise 
risk management, and institutional accountability.

 Division Leadership Responsibilities 

 Financial Leadership 

• Serve as the college’s chief financial officer and principal 
advisor to the President on financial strategy, fiscal 
sustainability, and institutional stewardship.

• Provide executive leadership for all financial operations, 
ensuring the integrity, transparency, and long-term health of 
the college’s financial resources.

• Deliver financial analysis and recommendations that support 
informed decision-making by the President, Cabinet, and Board of 
Regents.

• Through the Controller and Finance team, provide strategic 
oversight for:

• Budget development and administration

• Accounting and financial reporting

• Payroll administration

• Treasury, cash, investment, and debt management

• Annual financial audits and internal controls

• Financial forecasting and analysis

• Grant accounting and financial compliance

• State and federal financial reporting

• Financial systems and business process improvement

 Procurement and Administrative Services 

• Provide executive leadership for procurement and 
administrative support operations, ensuring services are 
efficient, compliant, transparent, and customer-focused.

• Promote responsible stewardship of public resources while 
supporting operational effectiveness and service to the college 
community.

• Through the Executive Director of Procurement and 
Administrative Services, oversee:

• Purchasing and procurement

• Contract administration and competitive solicitations

• Vendor relations

• Administrative services

• Auxiliary enterprises, including the campus bookstore, café, 
and merchandise store

• Shipping and receiving

 Facilities Management 

• Provide strategic leadership for the planning, maintenance, 
operation, preservation, and improvement of the college’s 
physical assets and campus environment.

• Ensure facilities remain safe, functional, attractive, and 
supportive of teaching, learning, student engagement, and 
community use.

• Through the Executive Director of Facilities Management, 
oversee:

• Facilities maintenance and operations

• Custodial services and utilities management

• Preventive and deferred maintenance

• Capital improvement, construction, and renovation projects

• Campus infrastructure

• Sustainability initiatives

• Space utilization and facilities planning

 Public Safety 

• Provide executive oversight of the school’s public safety and 
emergency preparedness functions, fostering a secure environment 
for learning and institutional operations.

• Collaborate with institutional leadership and external 
agencies to maintain a comprehensive approach to campus safety 
and emergency management.

• Through the Executive Director of Public Safety, oversee:

• Campus security

• Emergency preparedness and response

• Business continuity planning

• Safety compliance

• Threat assessment and risk mitigation

• Emergency communications and crisis response

 Minimum Qualifications 

 Required 

• Chartered Professional Accountant designation in good 
standing.

• Master’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, 
Accounting, Public Administration, Higher Education 
Administration, or a closely related field.

• At least eight years of progressively responsible executive 
leadership experience in finance and administration.

• At least three years of senior leadership experience within 
higher education, government, or another similarly complex 
organization.

• Demonstrated experience leading multiple administrative 
divisions and managing complex organizational budgets.

• Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership, manage 
organizational change, and build collaborative relationships 
across a complex organization.

 Preferred 

• Experience within an Ontario college or public higher 
education institution.

• Experience with public-sector budgeting, capital planning, and 
community college funding.

 Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities 

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to:

• Provide visionary executive leadership while maintaining 
strong fiscal stewardship.

• Develop and communicate long-term financial strategies that 
advance institutional priorities.

• Analyze complex financial and operational issues and develop 
practical, sustainable solutions.

• Build collaborative relationships across the institution and 
with external stakeholders.

• Lead organizational change with transparency, professionalism, 
and integrity.

• Interpret and apply applicable laws, regulations, accounting 
standards, and Board policies.

• Communicate effectively with the President, Board of Regents, 
executive leadership, faculty, staff, students, governmental 
officials, and community partners.

• Lead multiple complex operational areas while maintaining an 
institution-wide perspective.

• Develop high-performing leadership teams through coaching, 
mentoring, and succession planning.

• Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration, 
continuous improvement, and exceptional customer service.

• Exercise sound judgment and maintain the highest standards of 
ethics, professionalism, and confidentiality.

 The Opportunity

Reporting to the Vice President of Supply Chain & Strategy, this role is critical for building organizational planning capability to support sustainable, profitable growth.  It ensures alignment between business strategy and operational execution across production, procurement, and distribution.

 What You Bring

 Required

 Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority

 Knowledge/Skills/Abilities 

   Excellent analytical skills with an ability to manipulate large data sets and present analyses in a clear, concise manner 

   Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights for various groups of stakeholders 

   Demonstrated continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify metrics related to business processes, improving results through effective processes 

 Demonstrated proficiency in time management 

 What We Offer 

 Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)

 Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events

 A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition

 Opportunities for advancement and internal movement

 Education assistance for continuous skill development

 Academic scholarships for employees’ children

 Safety equipment and PPE support program

 Retirement savings and wellness initiatives

 Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 Inclusion and Accessibility 

 Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

 We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 Please note 

 Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

 Hiring Range: $134,996 - $168,745 per year. A candidate’s experience and knowledge may be factored into the pay a candidate receives for this position. This posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.description:
VP, Digital Experience & Growth 

 Job Type: Full time
 Location: Toronto
 Reporting to: CEO
 Role Type: New

 Goway Travel was founded in Toronto in 1970 by Bruce Hodge, a young Australian economist who moved to Canada to follow his dreams.

 From there, we have established ourselves as a global influence with offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila. While the travel industry endured major challenges, our strong foundations allowed Goway to forge ahead. We continually innovated, invested in new technology, and challenged the status quo.

 Still owned and operated by Bruce, with the support of his leadership board, our mission has always been to help our clients realize their travel dreams. Today, we are an industry-leading, global travel company with over 800 employees. Our team of experts utilizes cutting-edge technology to tailor-make 4 and 5-star travel experiences in over 100 countries around the world.

 At Goway Travel, we're not just a company; we're a family of dreamers and doers, inspired by our founder’s incredible journey. He didn't just follow a career path; he followed his heart, and in doing so, he built a company that helps others follow theirs.

 If you’re passionate about travel and innovation, we invite you to be a part of our exciting journey!

 Job Purpose:  

 As our first Vice President, Digital Experience & Growth, reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll own the digital growth engine end to end: the website, search, performance marketing, lifecycle, and the data that ties it all together. This is a rare seat where strategy and hands-on craft meet, and where your work shows up directly in revenue. 

 If you thrive in an environment where innovation meets real-world impact, this role offers the opportunity to shape the technology behind unforgettable journeys. 

 What will be your key responsibilities? 

 Own the vision, governance and performance of Goway’s web properties and portals, leading CRO, UX, merchandising and customer-journey improvements.

 Shape strategy across paid, organic search, referral and emerging channels, tying investment to revenue, profitability, lead quality and long-term customer value.

 Build lifecycle strategy for Direct travellers and Trade partners, including journeys, nurture programs, re-engagement flows, advisor communications, personalization, loyalty, retention and referral.

 Build reporting that links marketing activity and website performance to business results, and partner with Technology on segmentation, audience strategy, lead-quality analysis and customer data strategy.

 Required Skills and Qualifications:  

 15+ years of progressive leadership in digital marketing, digital product, e-commerce, lifecycle, growth, CRM, analytics or customer experience.

 A track record of leading digital transformation or growth initiatives that moved the numbers.

 Hands-on strength in website optimization, SEO, acquisition, conversion, personalization and retention.

 Deep fluency in CRM, journey orchestration, marketing automation, analytics and martech, with the ability to lead across Marketing, Technology, Sales and Operations.

 What can you expect from Goway? 
Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:

 We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.

 Your future matters to us, so we match your RRSP contributions and provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

 Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.

 Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.

 Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.

 Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 How to Apply: 
If this role feels like your next step, click "Apply Now" to create your profile, upload your CV, and share a few details about yourself. Our talent team reviews every application, and if your experience aligns with our needs, we will reach out to set up the next step.

 AI Screening Disclosure 
To help us fairly and efficiently review applications, we use an automated screening process to assess responses to pre-determined questions. This initial step ensures all candidates are evaluated consistently. Qualified applicants will be reviewed by our recruitment team for further consideration.

 Additional Notes 
Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

 Recruitment scams & fraud warning: 
Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

 About Goway 
Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 700 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. Discover more at goway.com.

Director, Technical Operations (Platform) 

 Job Type: Permanent Full Time
 Location: Hybrid - Toronto, Ontario
 Reporting to: Chief Technology Officer
 Salary: $160,000 – $190,000 CAD

 Job purpose 

 The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

 This is a practice-building role. You will define and own Goway's technical operations discipline: service levels, incident management, change control, observability and operational readiness, and you will make them the standard across our technology organisation. You will work alongside other Technology leaders. You will own the technology operations of our platform. You will have the CTO's mandate and backing to build the practice.

 What will be your key responsibilities? 

 Reliability and service management

 Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.

 Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.

 Own RCA and problem management.

 Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.

 Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.

 Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

 Integration and supplier platform operations

 Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.

 Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.

 Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.

 Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

 Platform and cloud operations

 Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.

 Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.

 Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.

 Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.

 Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

 Vendors, partners and compliance

 Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.

 Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.

 Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

 Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

 Substantial experience operating and governing third-party platforms and integrations, including holding vendors to service levels.

 Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.

 Ability to communicate operational risk and performance.

 Preferred

 Experience stabilising and operationalising new systems.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 Essential Duties and Responsibilities:  

 The Director FP&A and Capital Investment is a key member of the company’s finance team and is responsible for supporting all financial planning and analysis activities across the International Division of Top Aces Inc. The director will be responsible for the division’s annual budget process, financial forecasting, financial strategic planning and business performance analysis activities. Additionally, the director will be responsible for supporting the effort to enhance the company’s continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving profitability and efficiency. The director will provide project financial support, return on investment (ROI) analysis along with KPI development, measurement and analysis. The successful candidate will have demonstrable leadership competencies, strong attention to detail, and will work well under pressure in a fast-paced environment. The candidate will demonstrate a successful track record of working collaboratively in a dynamic environment and a matrix organizational structure.

 Own the division’s annual budgeting and financial planning process (quarterly forecasts and strategic plan 5-year forecast) and review all associated financial plans and budgets.

 Develop, lead, and manage core FP&A activities. 

 Lead the development of P&L, balance sheet and cash flow forecasts and partner with internal stakeholders to optimize working capital (prepayments, inventory) and cash flow generation.

 Lead the development of scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis and risks & opportunities. 

 Oversee capex financial management and capex forecasting improvement initiatives.

 Lead inventory financial management and work with key stakeholders to optimize the level of inventory.

 Oversee the preparation of the International Division monthly management accounts, FP&A reports and dashboards, including presentations to SLT and the company’s Board of Directors. 

 Support the division’s Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to evaluate and review new business and investment opportunities, including new business pricing, client Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), Return on Investment (ROI), payback period and return on capital (RONA) analyses.

 Support the executive team decision-making by providing insightful data and analysis with the objective of improving Top Aces’ profitability and efficiency.

 Build and develop the skill sets of finance professionals under her/his direction.

 Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:  

 Bachelor’s degree required with concentration in finance and/or accounting or comparable business field preferred.

 CPA and/or MBA preferred

 10-15 years of experience in relevant accounting, or financial leadership roles.

 Significant expertise with data analysis and reporting.

 Ability to handle multiple assignments on a timely basis with a high degree of accuracy.

 High level of motivation and aptitude for problem solving, with a strong attention to detail.

 Excellent interpersonal and communication skills as well as strategic thinking to effectively interface with external stakeholders and the division’s Senior Leadership Team.

 Ability to translate financial data into strategic insights.

 Able to work in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, possessing a high sense of urgency.

 Ability to perform all work in support of our Corporate Values of Excellence, Service, Integrity … Together.

 Working Conditions: 

 May be required to travel from time to time

 May be required to work overtime or longer hours when Top Aces Requires

 Supervisory, Training and Advisory Responsibilities: 

 May be required to provide regular guidance, advice and training, as requested by the supervisor, to other employees supporting the function.

 Occupational Health and Safety: 

 Employees are responsible for:

 Working in compliance with Occupational Health and Safety acts and regulations 

 Following safe work practices and procedures and using safeguards and personal protective equipment

 Reporting hazards (such as unsafe situations and activities) to their supervisor immediately.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

 Position requires Level II clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program

 By joining Top Aces, you will find: 

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

jobs.title: Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence
jobs.location: Canada; Dorval Head Office, Dorval, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

 We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 Position Summary 

 The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

 The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

 Top Aces Business Context 

 Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

 The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

 Key Responsibilities 

 Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model 

 Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.

 Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.

 Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.

 Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

 Data Governance Quality and Protection 

 Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.

 Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.

 Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.

 Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.

 Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

 Data Architecture Integration and Platforms 

 Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.

 Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.

 Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.

 Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.

 Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

 Aviation and MRO Data 

 Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.

 Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.

 Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.

 Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.

 Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

 Business Intelligence and Performance Management 

 Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.

 Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.

 Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.

 Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.

 Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

 Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence 

 Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.

 Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.

 Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.

 Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

 Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership 

 Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.

 Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.

 Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.

 Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.

 Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

 Education and Experience 

 Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.

 At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.

 Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.

 Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.

 Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

 Technical and Regulatory Knowledge 

 Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.

 Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.

 Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.

 Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.

 Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.

 Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

 Leadership Competencies 

 Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.

 Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.

 Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.

 Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.

 Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.

 Professional fluency in English is required. French and additional languages used across Top Aces' operations are assets.

 Measures of Success 

 Annual objectives will be established with the CIO and business leaders. Measures should demonstrate stronger control of critical data and visible improvements in how the company operates and makes decisions.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

 Position requires Level II clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program.

 By joining Top Aces, you will find: 

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

 Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

 Equal Employment Opportunity 

 At Top Aces, all employees are welcome regardless of race, nationality, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability or age. The masculine form may be used in this job description solely for ease of reading but refers to men, women and gender diversity.

jobs.title: Director, Product & Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Title: Director, Product & Strategy 
 Location: Hybrid (3 days per week) in Toronto / Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Ontario, Canada. 
Candidates must reside in Toronto or the GTA and be legally authorized to work in Canada.
 Travel: Approximately 10-20%
 Employment Type: Permanent, Full-Time
 Hiring Timeline: Immediate
 Reporting Line: Head of Tech Delivery 
 Existing Vacancy: Yes. This posting is for an existing vacancy. 
 Application Deadline: Open until filled. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

 Salary Range:  
 $140,000 - $160,000 CAD base per year, plus 15% bonus eligibility. 

 About Fulfillment IQ 
 Fulfillment IQ (FIQ) is a supply chain technology and consulting company helping retailers, brands, and 3PLs solve complex fulfillment and logistics challenges.
 Our work spans three core practices: Supply Chain Consulting, Technology Delivery & Transformation, and Implementation. We help customers assess and design supply-chain strategies, select and implement technology, modernize fulfillment operations, and build technology solutions that solve complex operational challenges.

 The Opportunity  
 We are looking for a Director, Product & Strategy to lead our Tech Delivery practice across both sides of the house: the internal teams that build, and the client relationships that fund and shape the work. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable in a client boardroom shaping strategy and in a delivery stand-up unblocking a team.
 You will own the arc of a client engagement end to end: understanding the business problem, shaping the solution strategy, and directing the cross-functional team that delivers it, all while continuously deepening and expanding the client relationship. You will also help incubate Fulfillment IQ's own internal innovation products, applying the same product discipline to what we build for ourselves.

 What You’ll Do 
 Client & Relationship Leadership 
 Own the client relationship as the senior point of contact for assigned clients, building trust with stakeholders from operators to executives.
 Capture and translate client needs into clearly framed problems and solution strategies, translating business goals into delivery roadmaps.
 Grow and expand accounts by identifying new opportunities, shaping proposals and statements of work, and converting successful delivery into expanded scope and long-term partnership.
 Manage expectations, scope, risks, and escalations proactively, keeping engagements healthy commercially and operationally.
 Delivery & Team Leadership 
 Lead and mentor cross-functional delivery teams, product managers, business analysts, UX designers, DevOps engineers, developers (front-end, back-end, full-stack), and tech leads.
 Direct delivery across engagements, planning, resourcing, quality, timelines, and budgets, and holding teams accountable to outcomes.
 Establish delivery standards, ways of working, and reusable practices that raise quality and predictability across the practice.
 Attract and develop talent, coaching leads, growing capability, and building a team people want to be part of.
 Product & Solution Strategy 
 Shape solution architectures and product strategies that fit each client's operations, budget, and roadmap.
 Incubate Fulfillment IQ's internal innovation products, owning discovery, prioritization, and delivery of what we build for our own IP and platforms.
 Translate supply chain and fulfillment technology trends into practical recommendations and differentiated offerings.
 Partner closely with sales, partnerships, and leadership to align solutions with market opportunity.

 What You'll Bring 
 8+ years of relevant experience, including leadership of technology delivery, product, or professional-services teams (services, consulting, systems-integration, or product backgrounds all welcome).
 Proven ability to manage senior client relationships and grow accounts, turning delivery success into expanded scope and revenue.
 Strong command of software delivery: product management, requirements, UX, and engineering across the full stack, plus modern DevOps and agile practices.
 Experience shaping solution strategy and translating ambiguous business problems into clear, deliverable roadmaps.
 A track record of leading and developing cross-functional teams and setting delivery standards.
 Supply chain, fulfillment, logistics, WMS/OMS/TMS, or e-commerce technology experience strongly preferred.
 Product ownership instincts: comfortable driving internal innovation products from idea to launch.
 Excellent communication and executive presence; able to move fluidly between strategy conversations and hands-on delivery.
 Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience; based in the US or Canada and able to work on a hybrid schedule.

Skills and Competencies 
 Required Skills 
 Client & stakeholder management: building and expanding senior relationships and negotiating scope.
 Delivery & program management: planning, resourcing, budgeting, risk management, and on-time execution across concurrent engagements.
 Solution & product strategy: framing ambiguous business problems and translating them into architectures and roadmaps.
 Cross-functional team leadership: directing product, BA, UX, engineering, and DevOps talent.
 Software delivery lifecycle fluency: agile/scrum, requirements, UX, and full-stack engineering across front-end, backend, and DevOps.
 Commercial acumen: proposals, statements of work, estimation, and account growth.
 Executive communication & presentation: clear, credible, and persuasive with technical and business audiences.
 Product ownership: prioritization, discovery, and driving products from concept to launch.
 Good-to-Have Skills 
 Supply chain / fulfillment domain: WMS, OMS, TMS, order management, or e-commerce logistics platforms.
 Pre-sales & solutioning: shaping deals and demonstrating solutions to prospective clients.
 Modern cloud & DevOps tooling: CI/CD, containers, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
 Product & delivery tooling: Jira, roadmapping, and agile management platforms.
 Data & analytics literacy: using metrics to steer delivery and inform product decisions.
 Relevant certifications: PMP, SAFe, CSM/CSPO, or equivalent.
 Nice-to-Have Skills 
 Experience at a technology consultancy, systems integrator, or 3PL/retail technology organization.
 Pre-sales / solutioning experience and familiarity with SOW and commercial models.
 Hands-on background in one or more delivery disciplines (product, engineering, UX, or DevOps).

 Why Fulfillment IQ  
 You will have the opportunity to help grow our implementation business, develop important client relationships, and contribute to how we approach the market. 
 Work with experienced implementation leaders who understand the platforms and the operations they support. 
 Sell services that address practical warehouse challenges and make a visible difference to clients. 
 Have a voice in account priorities, partner relationships, and the development of the practice. 
 Work with colleagues who value direct communication, sound judgment, and accountability. 
 Health and Wellness 
 Comprehensive extended health and dental coverage for you and your family
 Employee wellness programs where applicable
 Time Off 
 Competitive paid time off, sick leave, and public holidays
 Flexible leave policies that respect local labour standards
 Retirement and Financial Security 
 CPP contributions and a group retirement savings plan with employer contributions
 Employee stock options (ESOP), where applicable
 Professional Growth 
 Dedicated learning and development budget, with support for skills, leadership, and career progression
 Flexible Work 
 Remote and hybrid work options, flexible hours aligned to role and client needs
 Additional Perks 
 Equipment and workstation allowances, internet and business travel reimbursements, team events and offsites

 Work Authorization 
 Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada.
 Use of Artificial Intelligence in Hiring:  
 FIQ uses artificial intelligence to assist in the screening, assessment, and shortlisting of applications for this position, including features within our applicant tracking system. AI supports human reviewers and does not make hiring decisions on its own. Final hiring decisions are made by FIQ personnel. If you have questions about how AI is used in this process, contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com. 
 Accommodations:  
 FIQ is committed to an inclusive and accessible recruitment process. Consistent with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code, accommodations are available on request at any stage of recruitment and assessment. Contact hr@fulfillmentiq.com and we will work with you to meet your needs.

 Your personal information is collected and used for recruitment purposes in accordance with FIQ's Candidate Privacy Notice, available  here, and in accordance with applicable Canadian privacy law (PIPEDA). This includes the use of AI-assisted screening described above and cross-border storage or processing that may occur in the United States. By applying, you acknowledge this notice. Questions: hr@fulfillmentiq.com. 
 Equal Opportunity:  
 Fulfillment IQ is a people-first company built on trust, collaboration, and ownership. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and high-performing workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to any ground protected under the Ontario Human Rights Code, including race, ancestry, place of origin, colour, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, family status, or disability.

Founded in 2017, Unit8 is a fast-growing Swiss AI and data analytics consulting and services company dedicated to solving complex problems of traditional industries like automotive, chemical, financial services, manufacturing and pharma. We work with some of the biggest organisations in Europe to solve the challenges that directly affect their business - be it operations, finance, manufacturing or R&D.  Unit8’s mission is to drive the adoption of AI and Data Science in the non-digital industries and to help accelerate their digital transformation. Among its activities, Unit8 dedicates a part of its resources and time on projects that deeply matter to us - that includes collaboration on pro-bono and “engineering for good” causes. You can learn more about what we are passionate about at and on our you can find more useful information about our business and recruiting process.

 Are You the Leader We're Looking For?
 As a Managing Director at Unit8, success isn't just about closing deals — it's about becoming a cornerstone of how we grow and deliver in the Canadian market. You will own both sides of the equation: originating high-value client relationships and ensuring the work we deliver actually moves the needle for our clients. If you've built your career at the intersection of commercial impact and technical credibility, and you're ready to operate with real autonomy in an expert-led environment, this is the role.

 What Success Looks Like in This Role
 This is a senior leadership position for someone as comfortable originating a complex engagement as overseeing its delivery. You shape and close the deal, build relationships and trust, and you stay close enough to ensure the technical execution actually delivers value. You will succeed by:

 Building and converting a pipeline of high-value opportunities in the Canadian market — primarily in financial services — through a network earned over years of credible work in data & AI
 Selling from expertise: clients engage with you because you understand their problem because of your deep problem solving skills and experience not because you have a polished pitch
 Staying embedded in delivery long enough to set the right pace, challenge client assumptions, and keep teams focused on the actual business problem
 Bridging the gap between a senior data scientist and a C-suite conversation — translating technical constraints into strategic decisions and vice versa
 Raising the delivery bar by knowing what good looks like and holding teams to that standard

 What You'll Do
 Leverage your existing network to source, shape, and close high-value engagements in Canada (new logos, not just expansions)
 Translate complex business problems into concrete Data & AI solutions: identify where value can be created, make sure the team is building toward it, and hold the client accountable to realising it
 Lead and shape complex, tech-enabled transformations — from early problem definition through to scaled delivery — ensuring the right technology choices serve the business outcome, not the other way around
 Act as the senior point of contact for key clients throughout delivery, ensuring technical execution stays anchored to business value
 Challenge clients when necessary — on scope, pace, and ambition
 Work closely with our engineering and data science teams, providing business context, removing blockers and coaching them.

 We’re proud to be recognized as one of Fast Company’s Best Workplaces for Innovators and a 2025 Inc. Magazine Power Partner, awards that highlight how we’re redefining the future of logistics while empowering our partners to grow.
 Backed by leading Silicon Valley investors like Village Global, the fund whose investors include Bill Gates, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Reid Hoffman, and Sara Blakely, we’ve built a world-class team across the globe.
 We operate at scale but remain small enough for every person to have a massive impact. There’s a lot of important work ahead, and joining Burq means the opportunity to grow faster than ever while doing the most meaningful work of your career.

 Here’s a quick overview of what you will be doing:

 The Role
 We're looking for a Head of Data & AI to build the intelligence that powers Burq. 
 You'll build a world-class data-and-ML platform: the systems that turn data into models which make every delivery decision smarter and agents that automate the work the industry still does by hand. You'll set the strategy, make the hard architecture and modeling calls, ship models into production that move the business, and build the team to do it at scale.
 This is a player-coach role. You'll lead and grow the data and ML team while staying deeply hands-on — making architecture calls, reviewing engineering and modeling work, and ensuring the platform serves both product and business goals. You'll partner closely with the Head of Engineering, and with product and AI leadership on how intelligence shows up in the product.

 What You'll Do
 Data Platform

 Own the full data platform — the warehouse, streaming and batch ingestion, the semantic layer, and BI infrastructure.
 Define and enforce data governance — access management, quality standards, and a well-modeled, trustworthy "gold" layer.
 Make the warehouse the source of truth for operational, product, and financial analytics.

 Intelligence & Machine Learning 

 Build the models that power delivery intelligence — forecasting, prediction, optimization, matching/allocation, and reliability scoring that turn our data into better real-time decisions.
 Stand up the ML systems that make this real and reliable: feature pipelines, training, serving, evaluation, and drift monitoring.
 Design the learning loop — instrument decisions and outcomes so models continuously improve.
 Drive the AI agent initiative to production, partnering with product and engineering on the surrounding workflows.

 Team & Stakeholders

 Manage and grow the data and ML team (starting from a small core) — hire data engineers, analytics engineers, and data scientists/ML engineers as the platform matures.
 Establish a clear intake process for ad hoc data requests so the team works from a roadmap, not in reactive mode.
 Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Finance on data-driven analyses and decisions.
